analysis.investment_thesis: Mastek is a fundamentally sound IT services company with a strong 9-year CAGR track record, but at ₹5,412 Cr market cap it is firmly mid-cap — miles outside my SMILE sweet spot of 100–1,000 Cr. With promoter holding at just 35.8% and revenue growth decelerating sharply to ~7% in FY26, there is no multibagger catalyst visible from here.
key_strengths: Consistent FCF generation — ₹515 Cr in FY26, positive all 5 years; capital-light model works
Attractive valuation for an IT company — P/E 12.8x, EV/EBITDA 9.8x, D/E only 0.20
Strong 9-year profit CAGR of 32.5% shows the business did compound well historically
key_risks: Revenue growth collapsing — FY24: +19%, FY25: +13%, FY26: +7% — the deceleration is alarming
Promoter holding at 35.77% — far below my 50% minimum; low skin in the game
Finance costs ballooned from ₹4 Cr (2017) to ₹44 Cr (2024) before easing; acquisition-driven debt a concern
red_flags: Market cap ₹5,412 Cr — 5x above my upper limit of ~₹1,000 Cr; information asymmetry advantage is gone
DII at 19% + FII at 8% = already institutionally owned; no undiscovered angle left
Revenue growth slowing to single digits (7% FY26) — no inflection story, the opposite
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Mastek fails the SMILE screen on the most critical dimensions. At ₹5,412 Cr market cap and ₹3,699 Cr in revenue (P/S of 1.48x), this is a mid-cap IT services business — exactly the zone where my edge disappears. Institutions already own 27% combined (DII + FII), research coverage exists, and the information asymmetry that creates multibagger entries is absent. The promoter's 35.77% holding is a structural concern — when management doesn't own half the company, the alignment of interest weakens considerably.

The business fundamentals are respectable but not exciting for my framework. The 9-year revenue CAGR of 23.3% looks impressive, but the trajectory is bending sharply downward — FY26 grew revenue only 7% YoY. Operating margins at 14.1% are acceptable for a mid-tier IT services firm focused on Oracle Cloud and UK public sector, but there's no visible margin expansion story. Net profit of ₹404 Cr on ₹3,699 Cr revenue is a thin 10.9% net margin. From 100 rupees invested, I want 1,000 rupees back in 7–10 years — a decelerating mid-cap IT company at fair value cannot deliver that.
